age.evidence: Mice were 3 -4 months of age during the experimental protocol.

sex.evidence: 5-HTT KO mice (26 males and 27 females) and WT littermates (20 males and 26 females)

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg), provided by Usona Institute Inc., was dissolved in 0.9% saline solution, and administered via intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection.

handling.evidence: No explicit handling protocol described in methods.

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed in groups of 2 -5 same-sex mice in individually ventilated cages until weaning at four weeks of age, where they were then transferred to standard open-top boxes (34 × 16 × 16 cm; 2 -5 mice/box).

day_night_flipped.evidence: All behavioural testing was conducted during the light cycle (typically between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m.)... in a 12-hr light/dark cycle.

assays.assay_description: Locomotor activity measured for 15 min before and 60 min after acute psilocybin in a 26 x 26 x 38 cm photo-beam activity chamber; distance travelled analysed in 5-min bins.

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were acclimatised to their environment (room) for at least 30 min before testing; no separate apparatus habituation described, baseline used 10-15 min bin

setup_restrain.evidence: placing mice in a 26 x 26 × 38 cm photo-beam activity chamber

food_restriction.evidence: Standard activity chamber without food access.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard activity chamber without water access.

time_to_assay.evidence: Locomotor activity was measured for 15 min before and 60 min after acute psilocybin administration

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin (1 mg/kg i.p.) increased total distance travelled in WT mice but had no locomotor effect in 5-HTT KO mice. KO mice had higher baseline locomotion than WT.
outcomes.statistics: genotype × treatment interaction F(1,90)=18.18, p<0.0001, η2=0.083; WT-PSIL vs WT-SAL p<0.0001; KO-PSIL vs KO-SAL p=0.895; baseline genotype F(1,94)=21.03, p<0.001
outcomes.evidence: WT mice that were injected with psilocybin travelled more than WT mice that received saline (p<0.0001). Psilocybin compared to saline did not alter locomotor activity in 5-HTT KO mice (p=0.895).

B1_num_measures.evidence: we analysed distance travelled (cm) via 5-min bins

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: we analysed distance travelled (cm) via 5-min bins

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: no transition or sequence analysis reported

B4_ethological.evidence: distance travelled / locomotion is not ethological per rubric

D1_continuity.evidence: pre/post recording continuous on a single day

D2_session_duration.evidence: 15 min before and 60 min after acute psilocybin administration (~75 min continuous)

D4_baseline.evidence: We used the 10-15-min bin before injection as baseline

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in the locomotor cell and video recorded from above for 15 min immediately post-injection; head-twitches manually scored by a blinded researcher and analysed in 5-min bins.

setup_habituation.evidence: Only 30 min room acclimation described; no apparatus habituation before HTR

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in the locomotor cell and were video recorded from a top view

food_restriction.evidence: No food in apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water in apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: in the 15 min immediately after injection

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin induced robust head-twitches in WT mice, with the response completely absent in 5-HTT KO mice across 5, 10 and 15 min bins. No significant sex difference.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin induced a greater number of head-twitches in WT mice compared to KO mice (F1,45 = 2.88; p < 0.0001)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: analyse head-twitch responses in 5-min bins for the first 15 min

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually scored by a blinded and trained researcher

D2_session_duration.evidence: in the 15 min immediately after injection

assays.assay_description: 10-min test in a 26 × 26 × 38 cm TruScan arena divided into light (750 lux) and dark compartments; percentage time in light, distance travelled and latency measured. Tested at 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days after psilocybin.

setup_habituation.evidence: Only 30 min room acclimation; no apparatus habituation described

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were allowed to explore the arena for 10 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in apparatus during test

water_restriction.evidence: No water in apparatus during test

time_to_assay.evidence: Anxiety-like behaviour was measured via the LDB at three-time points: 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days after acute psilocybin injection.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin did not significantly change time in the light compartment in either sex/genotype, though a non-significant trend toward an anxiolytic effect appeared in WT females (p=0.09). KO mice showed reduced light duration vs WT.
outcomes.statistics: Females: treatment F(1,49)=3.23, p=0.078; genotype F(1,49)=96.05, p<0.0001. Males: genotype × time F(2,84)=8.08, p<0.001; treatment F(1,42)=0.43, p=0.514
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin did not significantly alter the time spent in the light compartment (p=0.078). Psilocybin did not alter light duration in male WT or KO animals (p=0.514).

B1_num_measures.evidence: % time in light, total distance travelled, latency to the light side

B4_ethological.evidence: time in zone is a spatial measure, not ethological

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Activity Monitor software (Med Associates) - position tracking

E2_shelter.evidence: dark compartment is fully enclosed (per rubric)

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into light and dark compartments with a black Plexiglas insert

D1_continuity.evidence: measured at three-time points: 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days

D3_recording_days.evidence: 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days = 3 recording days

D5_followup.evidence: tests at 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days after injection

assays.assay_description: 6-min swim in a 2-L beaker filled with 1.5 L of 25°C water; immobility scored in the last 4 min using Depression Scan (Clever Sys). Tested at 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days after psilocybin.

setup_habituation.evidence: Immediately after the LDB, mice were habituated to the PST room for 30 min (room only, not apparatus)

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in a 2-L beaker filled with 1.5 L of water, from which escape was impossible (FST cylinder - per rubric)

water_restriction.evidence: No drinkable water access during swim

time_to_assay.evidence: Testing was conducted over three time points: the first time point was at 24 h, the second was at 72 h, and the third was 8 days after drug administration.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin did not significantly alter immobility time in either genotype or sex; a non-significant trend for a genotype × treatment interaction (p=0.069) and treatment effect in WT females (p=0.054) was noted. KO mice exhibited increased immobility vs WT.
outcomes.statistics: Females: genotype F(1,49)=23.05, p<0.0001; genotype × treatment F(1,49)=3.47, p=0.069; treatment trend WT females p=0.054. Males: genotype F(1,42)=50.09, p<0.0001; treatment F(1,42)=0.003, p=0.954
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin did not alter immobility time in either KO or WT mice (p=0.954). A trend for a genotype × treatment interaction was observed in females (p=0.069).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Time spent immobile was the main outcome measured

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Immobility duration in the last 4 min scored as total

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility is explicitly excluded per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Depression Scan, Clever Sys - position-based tracking (per rubric SCORE 0)

E1_environment_type.evidence: 2-L beaker filled with 1.5 L of water

E7_social_context.evidence: Male and female mice were placed in different beakers

E8_food_water.evidence: no food/drinkable water access during swim

D1_continuity.evidence: Testing was conducted over three time points: 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days

D3_recording_days.evidence: 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days = 3 recording days

D5_followup.evidence: 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days after drug administration

assays.assay_description: Individually housed mice given 0.1% saccharin and tap water bottles (alternated positions) over 24-h periods across 3 days, starting on day 8 post-psilocybin; preference calculated as % of total fluid intake.

setup_habituation.evidence: We did not habituate mice to their single-housed environment, as we intended to maximise stress effects

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were individually housed and exposed to both 0.1% saccharin and tap water solutions

food_restriction.evidence: Mice had ad libitum access to standard chow

water_restriction.evidence: exposed to both 0.1% saccharin and tap water solutions across a 24-h period

time_to_assay.evidence: On the 8th day after psilocybin administration ... exposed to both 0.1% saccharin and tap water solutions across a 24-h period for three days.

outcomes.summary: Female 5-HTT KO mice exhibited reduced saccharin preference compared with female WT, indicating an anhedonia-like phenotype. Psilocybin did not alter saccharin preference in either sex/genotype.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin did not alter saccharin preference in WT or KO mice (p=0.483). Female 5-HTT KO mice exhibited reduced saccharin preference compared to WT mice (p<0.01).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Saccharin-preference scores were calculated as a percentage of total fluid intake

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: preference computed per 24-h day; effect of time is between-session

B4_ethological.evidence: preference score is not an ethological act

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were individually housed and exposed to both 0.1% saccharin and tap water solutions

E3_bedding.evidence: bedding presence in home cage not explicitly stated for test

E8_food_water.evidence: exposed to both 0.1% saccharin and tap water solutions; ad libitum chow

D1_continuity.evidence: 24-h continuous bottle-intake monitoring across three consecutive days

D2_session_duration.evidence: across a 24-h period for three days

D5_followup.evidence: On the 8th day after psilocybin administration

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same five behavioural assays (Locomotor, HTR, LDB, PST, SPT). No assays merged or dropped.

D2 for Locomotor set to 2 (61 min–6 h) since the continuous recording spans 15 min baseline + 60 min post-injection (~75 min total continuous session); qwen and glm scored 1, but gptoss's 2 better reflects the continuous duration.
B7 for PST set to 0: Depression Scan (Clever Sys) is position-based tracking per rubric (similar to TopScan).

C2 setup_habituation set to 'no' across assays: paper only describes room acclimation (30 min), explicitly not apparatus habituation. glm's 'yes' overcounted room acclimation as apparatus habituation.
PST setup_restrain set to 'yes' per rubric explicit example listing FST cylinder as restraint.
Day/night flipped set to 'no' (not 'not_reported'): paper explicitly states testing during the light cycle (9am-4pm) under a 12-hr light/dark cycle.
SPT D1 upgraded to 'Continuous monitoring' (score 2): three consecutive 24-h continuous bottle intake measurements satisfy ≥6 h continuous criterion.
